$comment: THE MOVEMENT CATALOGUE. One entry per JOB the programme needs done, and every way of doing that
job in HIS gym, with the station each way lives at.
WHY IT REPLACES muscles.json, written four hours earlier the same day. That file listed the 34
exercises the programme happened to contain and asked whether every muscle was covered. He spotted
the circularity immediately: 'you are going about the list that we already have, but how do we know
if that list is complete?' Coverage measured against the exercises already chosen can only ever
come back complete. The closed set to measure against is not the exercise list, it is
equipment.json: THE GYM IS FINITE AND KNOWN. scripts/gym-catalogue.mjs checks this file against it.
AND WHY VARIANTS ARE FIRST-CLASS, his second point: 'there is a lot of lifts that can be done in
different ways, barbell, dumbbell, cable, and they will still be the same exercise basically... if
I am about to do a straight-arm pulldown and I was going to pair that with something for biceps,
you might as well [do] the cable [curl] instead of' walking to the dumbbells.
That is a real scheduling constraint and nothing in this repo could express it. program.json
carried 86 `alts` spread across 50 slots, which produced exactly the drift a per-slot list always
produces: `tricep-pushdown` and `tricep-pushdown-alt`, `assisted-pullup` and `lat-pulldown-alt`,
`bicep-curl` and `db-curl-supinated`, `hammer-curl` and `db-hammer-curl`, `suitcase-carry` and
`suitcase-carry-upper`. Five pairs of ids for the same movement, because a slot-local alternative
list has nowhere to say 'this is the same lift somewhere else'.
STRUCTURE. A movement owns the muscles. A variant owns the implement, the zone and the station,
and may override the muscles only where the mechanics genuinely differ (front squat against back
squat, overhead extension against pushdown). Everything else is inherited, so a muscle attribution
is written once and cannot drift between four days.
THREE KINDS OF CLAIM, tagged, because conflating them is how this project got 91 false claims in
one audit:
anatomy     which muscles a movement uses. Textbook, not a trial finding. Never cite a study.
evidence    this variant beats another for a stated purpose, with a fetched source.
convention  standard practice, no trial. Most variant choices are honestly this.
unsourced   no basis at all, and it says so.
WHETHER A VARIANT IS CURRENTLY PRESCRIBED IS NOT STORED HERE, AND MAY NOT BE. There was an
`inProgramme` boolean on all 103 variants until 2026-08-27. It was already wrong on nine of them
the day the file shipped: the same session's rebuild edited program.json and never touched the
flags, so db-rdl read false while being prescribed and pushup read true after being cut. Its only
consumer was the `*` marker in gym-catalogue.mjs --options, which is the very view the handoff
pointed the next agent at.
This is the workspace's own stale-copy disease (body metrics 2026-08-01, immigration 2026-08-11)
reproduced inside one repo on day one: every copy of a fact is a fact that goes stale silently.
So the copy is deleted rather than corrected. program.json is the only place that says what is
prescribed, and gym-catalogue.mjs derives the marker from it at read time. content/gym/validate.mjs
refuses the key if anyone reintroduces it, because a comment saying 'do not add this back' does
not execute. `false` never meant rejected anyway: it meant available and unused, which is what a
variant's presence in this file already says.

squat-bilateral.name: Bilateral squat
squat-bilateral.note: Also the reason no hip thrust is needed: Plotkin 2023 found squat and hip thrust produce similar gluteal hypertrophy, and the squat adds quads and adductors.
squat-bilateral.source: Plotkin DL et al. Front Physiol. 2023;14:1279170. Evidence file section 13.

variants.name: Front Squat
variants.note: More quad-dominant and more trunk than the back squat, which is why it is a genuinely different lift with its own weight and its own history rather than a lighter copy.

variants.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
variants.note: Capped by what he can hold at the chest, so it ceilings well below a barbell squat.

variants.name: Leg Press
variants.note: In the gym, never prescribed, never logged. No erector or trunk demand, which makes it the one bilateral squat option that pairs freely.

squat-unilateral.name: Single-leg squat
squat-unilateral.note: Single-leg loading without a rack, so every variant holds no fixture and can pair with anything.

variants.name: Reverse Lunge
variants.note: NO REASON RECORDED for having this AND the split squat. They train the same thing.

variants.name: Smith Split Squat
variants.note: Removes the balance ceiling, so the legs limit the set instead of the balance.

variants.name: Cossack Squat
variants.note: Frontal plane and single leg at once.

hinge-bilateral.name: Bilateral hip hinge
hinge-bilateral.note: The loadable posterior chain. The RDL biases hamstrings; a conventional deadlift produces greater glute and quadriceps activation.
hinge-bilateral.source: Lee S et al. J Exerc Sci Fit. 2018;16(3):87-93. EMG, directional only.

variants.name: BB Deadlift
variants.note: HE HAS ALREADY DONE ONE: 2026-08-05 ramped 180x6, 200x6, 225x4 and it was logged under romanian-deadlift by mistake. That is the only conventional-deadlift data that exists. Not currently prescribed, and mentioning it is not a reason to prescribe it: see evidence file 20.8 item 7.

variants.name: DB Romanian Deadlift
variants.note: Holds no fixture, so unlike the barbell RDL it can pair with anything. Ceilings at the heaviest pair of dumbbells he can hold.

variants.name: Good Morning
variants.note: Logged 6 sets in May and June at up to 95 lb, then dropped with no reason recorded.

variants.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
variants.note: Logged 13 sets at up to 50 lb, last used 2026-08-08. Loadable by hugging a plate.

variants.name: KB Swing
variants.note: Ballistic hinge. Trains the hinge fast rather than heavy, so it does not substitute for the RDL.

variants.name: Single-Leg RDL
variants.note: Capped by balance rather than by the hamstrings, stuck at 40 lb, which is why it has never progressed.

variants.name: B-Stance RDL
variants.note: The back toe stays down, which removes the balance ceiling that stalls the single-leg version.

knee-flexion.name: Knee flexion (hamstring isolation)
knee-flexion.note: SOURCE VOID. Its only citation was the Motion Blueprint guide, dropped 2026-08-27.

knee-extension.name: Knee extension (quad isolation)
knee-extension.note: IN THE GYM, NEVER PRESCRIBED, NEVER LOGGED. Listed so the gap is visible rather than invisible. Holds a fixture.

hip-extension-isolation.name: Hip extension isolation
hip-extension-isolation.note: Plotkin 2023 argues AGAINST needing this at all while he squats twice a week.
hip-extension-isolation.source: Plotkin DL et al. Front Physiol. 2023;14:1279170.

variants.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
variants.note: NOT LOADABLE, so it can never progress. On all four days by accretion, never by a decision.

variants.name: Smith Hip Thrust
variants.note: The loadable version. The gym has no hip thrust machine; the Smith is the recorded workaround.

adduction.name: Adduction and frontal plane
adduction.note: Loaded frontal-plane work rather than a band, because Comert and Gruber 2025 found hip strengthening alone had minimal effect on knee alignment.
adduction.source: Comert and Gruber 2025. Evidence file section 5.

variants.name: Copenhagen Plank
variants.note: Progressed by lever length, not weight, so the app's ladder does not apply to it.

variants.name: Side Plank w/ Leg Lift
variants.note: On the floor, so it holds nothing, where the Copenhagen it was aliased to holds the bench. Muscles are inherited from the movement exactly as the alias inherited them, so nothing about the volume count changes.

calf.name: Calf raise
calf.note: SOURCE VOID for its placement. The Motion Blueprint guide was the only basis for where it sits.

variants.name: Machine Calf Raise
variants.note:
HIS RULING, 2026-08-28: "the calf raise thing I swapped to machine calf raise, so it was not DB
calf raise." It was called Standing Calf Raise and the SLOT copy said "DB Standing Calf Raise",
which is what sent him looking for an alternative that said Machine. There was one, and it was an
alias of this same variant, so choosing it logged a second exercise_id for one movement: twelve
bodyweight sets here, three sets at 180 to 210 lb there, and the card read the first and offered
him about 5 lb.

`machine-calf-raise` stays an ALIAS so those three sets still resolve to this variant, and
src/lib/gym/equivalent-ids.ts makes every history read follow aliases. The redundant alt is gone.

variants.name: DB Calf Raise
variants.note: Holds no fixture, so it can ride in any rest gap. The machine version cannot.

push-horizontal.name: Horizontal press

variants.name: DB Bench Press
variants.note: At 75 lb dumbbells he presses 150 lb, against a 185 lb BARBELL bench he logged on 2026-05-25 before it was dropped with no reason recorded. This is the lift that has moved least.

variants.name: BB Bench Press
variants.note: Logged 6 sets to 185 lb in May and early August, then dropped. Higher ceiling and a finer load step than the dumbbells.

variants.name: Pushup
variants.note: Added 2026-08-27 as an upper primer and refuted the same day. Not a plyometric, and post-activation enhancement is measured on jumps and sprints, never on a following strength set. It pre-fatigues the press behind it.

push-horizontal.$tricepsNote: TRICEPS ARE A SYNERGIST HERE, NOT AN AGONIST, and they were primary until 2026-08-29. He found it by reading the volume table: "How come bench press, seated DB overhead press, machine chest press, and machine shoulder press are fully counting for triceps?" THE PROOF IS INTERNAL. Every PULL in this file already counts its arm muscle as a synergist: pull-horizontal and pull-vertical both list biceps under secondary. Every PUSH counted its arm muscle in full. Same anatomical relationship, two different rules, and nothing but this table would ever have shown it. Pelland 2026 defines the fractional method by target: a direct set targets the muscle, an indirect set targets it as a secondary or synergist muscle and counts 0.5. The agonist of a bench press is the pectoralis major and of an overhead press the anterior deltoid; the triceps assist both. WHAT IT COST: triceps read 22 fractional sets a week against an efficient zone topping at 10, and that number was the whole basis of the advice to drop the overhead extension. The real figure is 15.5. The two-agonist entries elsewhere in this file are NOT the same case and stay: a squat extends the knee and the hip, so quadriceps and glutes are both agonists, and a row is both a shoulder extension and a scapular retraction. One movement, two prime movers is real; one movement, a prime mover plus the arm that assists it is not.

chest-isolation.name: Chest fly
chest-isolation.note: IN THE GYM, NEVER PRESCRIBED. The pec deck also runs backwards as a rear-delt machine, which is a second unused option.

push-vertical.name: Vertical press
push-vertical.note: Its sole citation, Nunes 2021, could not be verified. This is also the ONLY main lift whose estimated 1RM has fallen, and the cause is a load step it cannot reach.

variants.name: Seated DB Overhead Press
variants.note:
Stuck: at 65 lb the jump to 70 demands more than the top of its rep range banks.

IT WAS CALLED "Standing DB Overhead Press" UNTIL 2026-08-28 AND HE HAS NEVER DONE IT STANDING. His note #26 at the rack: "Also whatever history is on standing db has always been seated, ive never done standing db", and #25: "Standing db overhead is not really practical either Standing barbell or seated db". Twenty sets of history sit under this id going back to 2026-05-26, all of them seated, and the logged rows are stamped "DB Overhead Press" with no "Standing" in them: the word was added by the catalogue and never by him.

So the station is `bench` now, not null. That is not cosmetic. A null station means the exercise holds no fixture and can partner anything, which is how a seated press could have been paired with something that needs the bench. His name for it is the true one.

WHETHER THE PROGRAMME SHOULD KEEP SEATED DUMBBELLS OR MOVE TO A STANDING BARBELL IS HIS CALL, and it is parked as an open question on this variant. Renaming records what he has been doing; it does not decide what he should do.

open.q: You said standing DB overhead is not practical, and offered two alternatives: standing barbell, or seated DB. The card now says Seated DB, which is what your twenty logged sets actually were, so nothing is mislabelled any more. The programme question is separate and it is yours. (a) KEEP SEATED DB. Cost: nothing changes, your 65 lb history carries straight through, and it stays stuck where the note above says it is stuck, because the next dumbbell up is a jump the rep range cannot bank. (b) STANDING BARBELL. Cost: it moves to the rack, so it stops being pairable with anything in the dumbbell area, and it starts from a separate history (`bb-ohp` holds 3 sets at 115 lb from 2026-08-04). The upside is the one that matters: a barbell goes up in 5 lb steps, which is the ladder problem this lift has had all year. Which one?

variants.name: BB Overhead Press
variants.note: Logged to 105 lb in May and June, then dropped. A barbell moves in 5 lb total, which is a 2.5 lb step per side against the dumbbells' 5 lb per hand.

pull-horizontal.name: Horizontal pull (row)
pull-horizontal.note: A bent-over row is also the largest trunk brace in the week, which is why pairing it with dead bugs is redundant rather than complementary.
pull-horizontal.source: CONVENTION for selection; the pairing point is Zhang 2025, evidence file section 12.

variants.name: Seated Cable Row
variants.note: Moves in 2.5 lb steps, the finest increment anywhere in this gym.

variants.name: Chest-Supported DB Row
variants.note: No erector or trunk cost, because the chest is supported. That makes it the row that pairs freely.

variants.name: Assisted Pull-Up
variants.note: Assistance moves in 10 lb steps off 40 lb, a 25% change, which is why it cannot reach its next rung.

variants.name: Pull-Up (Smith section bar)
variants.note: Second bar in the gym. Listed so no station is unreachable, not because a second pull-up bar changes anything.

lat-isolation.name: Shoulder extension (lat isolation)
lat-isolation.note: Adds lat volume without adding biceps volume, because the elbow does not bend.

variants.name: Band Straight-Arm Pulldown
variants.note: A band anchored high on a rack post, which OCCUPIES that rack: see the band-anchored entry in equipment.json. It was aliased to the cable version, so the catalogue placed it at the high pulley across the gym.

rear-delt.name: Horizontal shoulder abduction (rear delts)
rear-delt.note: No source anywhere justifies its current four exposures a week.

variants.name: DB Reverse Fly
variants.note: Its 20 lb dumbbell steps 25% to the next weight, so it cannot progress.

variants.name: Cable Reverse Fly
variants.note: 2.5 lb steps, which fixes the unreachable-weight problem the dumbbell version has.

variants.name: Face Pull
variants.note: Logged 6 sets in May and June at up to 35 lb, then dropped.

side-delt.name: Shoulder abduction (side delts)
side-delt.note: The only direct work the side delts get. No source justifies four exposures a week.

variants.name: DB Lateral Raise
variants.note: Stuck at a 25% load step from 20 lb to 25 lb.

variants.name: Seated DB Lateral Raise
variants.note: Seated, so it holds the bench. Was an alias of the standing raise until 2026-08-27, which made the catalogue say it holds no fixture while program.json correctly said bench.

variants.name: Cable Lateral Raise
variants.note: 2.5 lb steps. This is the fix for the unreachable next weight, per evidence file section 17.

variants.name: KB Lateral Raise
variants.note:
Kettlebells instead of dumbbells. Worth its own history precisely because this lift is the one stuck on a 25 percent load step from 20 to 25 lb: a different implement is a different ladder, and merging the two would hide which one stalled.

PROMOTED FROM AN ALIAS OF db-lateral-raise ON 2026-08-28. It was offered as an alt on a slot whose own exercise it resolved to, which is a choice between an exercise and itself: picking it wrote a second exercise_id for one movement and split the weight history. It had never been picked, so nothing needed migrating. validate.mjs refuses that shape now.

elbow-flexion.name: Elbow flexion (biceps)
elbow-flexion.note: Kassiano 2022: variation helps when variants load the muscle DIFFERENTLY and may hinder when they are redundant. Swapping implement at the same shoulder position is the redundant kind. Changing where the SHOULDER sits is the systematic kind, which is why the incline and preacher entries carry a note and the rest do not.
elbow-flexion.source: Kassiano W et al. J Strength Cond Res. 2022. Evidence file section 14.

variants.name: Cable Curl
variants.note: HIS OWN EXAMPLE, 2026-08-27: if the block before it is a straight-arm pulldown, this keeps him at the cable stack instead of walking to the dumbbells. 2.5 lb steps as well.

variants.name: EZ Bar Preacher Curl
variants.note: SHOULDER FLEXED, so the biceps work shortened. Genuinely different from a standing curl, and therefore the systematic kind of variation. MISPLACED though: he asked on 2026-08-15 for the EZ bar as a SWAP on the dumbbell curl card, and the next commit made it Friday's lead.

variants.name: Incline DB Curl
variants.note: SHOULDER EXTENDED, so the biceps work lengthened. The genuine opposite of the preacher curl, and the one pairing of curls that is not redundant.

elbow-extension.name: Elbow extension (triceps)
elbow-extension.note: Same logic as the curls: shortened against lengthened is systematic variation, one handle against another is redundant.
elbow-extension.source: Kassiano W et al. J Strength Cond Res. 2022.

variants.name: Tricep Pushdown
variants.note: Shoulder neutral, long head SHORTENED. 2.5 lb steps.

variants.name: DB Overhead Tricep Extension
variants.note: Shoulder flexed, long head LENGTHENED, which is what makes this and the pushdown non-redundant. CAVEAT: the meta-analysis favouring longer muscle length studied quadriceps in five of eight trials and no triceps, so applying it here extrapolates across muscles.
variants.source: Strey B, Irigoyen A, McMahon G, Pinto RS. Sport Sci Health. 2025;22(33):1-14. DOI 10.1007/s11332-025-01586-5. Eight studies, longer length ES 0.283 p=0.036. EXTRAPOLATED to triceps.

variants.name: Cable Overhead Tricep Extension
variants.note: Same lengthened position as the dumbbell version, at the cable stack and in 2.5 lb steps.

anti-rotation.name: Anti-rotation trunk
anti-rotation.note: SOURCE VOID. The 'eight core patterns' claim behind the Pallof press came from the Motion Blueprint guide.

variants.name: Half-Kneeling Cable Pallof Press
variants.note:
Half-kneeling rather than standing. Same station and same cable, and it is a harder anti-rotation position that takes less weight to load, so sharing one weight history with the standing version would read as a regression every time he knelt down.

PROMOTED FROM AN ALIAS OF cable-pallof ON 2026-08-28. It was offered as an alt on a slot whose own exercise it resolved to, which is a choice between an exercise and itself: picking it wrote a second exercise_id for one movement and split the weight history. It had never been picked, so nothing needed migrating. validate.mjs refuses that shape now.

variants.name: Dead Bug
variants.note: NOT LOADABLE. 9 sets a week, more than any main lift, and it sits in the rest gap of a bent-over row, which is already the largest trunk brace in the week.

variants.name: Hanging Knee Raise
variants.note: Logged 6 sets in August. Progressed by leg position rather than weight.

variants.name: Cable Crunch
variants.note: THE ONLY LOADABLE TRUNK OPTION in the gym. Every trunk exercise currently prescribed is bodyweight and therefore cannot progress.

carry.name: Loaded carry
carry.note: The only bare-handed grip work in the week, which is the stated reason straps are permitted on the RDL.

variants.name: Suitcase Carry
variants.note: Single-side, so it adds anti-lateral-flexion that the two-sided farmer carry does not.

variants.name: KB Suitcase Hold
variants.note:
A kettlebell in one hand instead of a dumbbell. Same anti-lateral-flexion job, different handle and a different weight ladder, so it earns its own history rather than sharing one.

PROMOTED FROM AN ALIAS OF suitcase-carry ON 2026-08-28. It was offered as an alt on a slot whose own exercise it resolved to, which is a choice between an exercise and itself: picking it wrote a second exercise_id for one movement and split the weight history. It had never been picked, so nothing needed migrating. validate.mjs refuses that shape now.

variants.name: DB Static Hold
variants.note: Heavy dumbbells held at the sides, standing still rather than walking, for when the floor is too crowded to carry. PROMOTED FROM AN ALIAS OF farmer-carry ON 2026-08-28. It was offered as an alt on the farmer carry slot while resolving to that same variant, which is a choice between an exercise and itself: picking it would have written a second exercise_id for one movement and split the history, the way the calf raise did. It also progresses on TIME where the carry progresses on distance, so one shared history could not have described both. Never picked, so nothing needed migrating.

plyo-vertical.name: Vertical plyometric
plyo-vertical.note: In the programme because plyometric training is worth doing at 2 to 3 sessions a week, NOT because it primes the lift after it. Post-activation enhancement is measured on jumps and sprints, never on a following strength set.
plyo-vertical.source: Deng N et al. Sci Rep. 2024;14:11272. 21 studies, 1,263 untrained participants, strength ES 0.61. Evidence file section 4 and 15.

variants.name: Box Jump
variants.note: He has swapped to this from broad jump every single time, 20 sets since 2026-06-09. Lower-impact landing at his bodyweight because he steps down.

variants.name: Broad Jump
variants.note: REMOVED as a default. He has swapped away from it every time and has said it does not fit a crowded commercial gym.

plyo-lateral.name: Frontal-plane plyometric
plyo-lateral.source: Deng N et al. Sci Rep. 2024;14:11272. Evidence file section 4.

hip-abduction.name: Hip abduction (glute medius)
hip-abduction.note: Glute MEDIUS rather than maximus, so it is not covered by the squat the way hip extension is. It was in the programme until 2026-08-16 as a banded lateral walk and was removed for the right reason: Comert and Gruber 2025 found hip strengthening ALONE had minimal effect on knee alignment. The loaded frontal-plane work replaced it. Listed here so the removal stays visible and so the cable option is on record.
hip-abduction.source: Comert and Gruber 2025. Evidence file section 5.

variants.name: Banded Lateral Walk
variants.note: Logged 12 sets to 2026-08-05, then removed.

variants.name: Clamshell
variants.note: Currently in the WARM-UP, not the programme body.

variants.name: Cable Hip Abduction
variants.note: The only LOADABLE abduction option in the gym. The band versions cannot progress.
